# Preface {.unnumbered}

This book collects notes on multilevel and longitudinal models, written for applied researchers in education and the social sciences. It grew out of S-043 at the Harvard Graduate School of Education.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Work in progress
This is a draft and will be updated over time.
:::

## Who this book is for

Readers who are comfortable with ordinary regression and want to know what changes when observations come in groups: students in schools, patients in hospitals, repeated measures in people. We assume familiarity with R, but the focus is on what the models *mean*, not on syntax.

## How each chapter is organized

Every chapter follows the same shape, so you always know where to look:

- **The chapter in one paragraph.** The whole argument, before the details.
- **The main text.** Built around a single running example, with every equation tied to R code and every number in the output used in a sentence.
- **Vocabulary decoder and common mistakes.** The field uses many names for the same thing; these sections sort them out.
- **Quick reference.** The formulas, on one screen.
- **Worked examples and self-check.** Questions with answers hidden until you want them.

## The running dataset

The first several chapters share one dataset of grade 3 students' reading comprehension scores, nested in schools. Each chapter layers new complexity onto the same data, so the models can be compared directly.

## Software

All models are fit in R with `lme4`:

``` r
install.packages("lme4")
library(lme4)
```
